record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: What additional non-perturbative information about boundary and defect conformal field theories can supersymmetry provide, including through techniques such as supersymmetric localization?

evidence.quote: What more can SUSY tell us about bCFTs and dCFTs, for example via SUSY localization?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{CFT}_d$ be a $d$-dimensional conformal field theory and let $\mathcal{D}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a conformal boundary or a conformal defect of dimension $p<d$ that preserves the subgroup $SO(p+1,1)\times SO(d-p)$ of the conformal group. The defect data of $(\mathrm{CFT}_d,\mathcal{D})$ consist of:
\begin{itemize}
\item the bulk one-point functions $\langle \mathcal{O}_\Delta(x)\rangle_\mathcal{D} = a_\mathcal{O}/|x_\perp|^\Delta$ for bulk primaries $\mathcal{O}_\Delta$,
\item the spectrum $\{\widehat{\Delta}_i\}$ of defect primary operators and their bulk-to-defect coupling coefficients $b_{\mathcal{O}\,\widehat{\mathcal{O}}}$,
\item the defect conformal anomaly coefficients (e.g.\ for $p=2$ the central charges $b$ and $d_1,d_2$, and for $p=4$ the anomalies $a_\mathcal{D}$, $c_\mathcal{D}$, $d_{1,2}$),
\item the defect free energy / $g$-function and its monotonicity along defect RG flows.
\end{itemize}

Now suppose in addition that the bulk theory and the defect together preserve some amount of supersymmetry, so that supersymmetric-localization techniques apply (in particular, that the path integral on a suitable curved background such as $S^d$, $S^p\times \mathbb{H}^{d-p}$, or $\mathbb{HS}^d$ in the presence of $\mathcal{D}$ can be reduced to a finite-dimensional matrix integral).

Determine which of the non-perturbative defect data above can be computed exactly using supersymmetric localization in the presence of the defect $\mathcal{D}$. Concretely, formulate and answer the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For which classes of supersymmetric defects (e.g.\ BPS Wilson/'t Hooft lines, surface operators, BPS boundaries and interfaces of class $D5$/$NS5$ type, codimension-two monodromy defects) does localization on $S^d$ produce a closed-form matrix model whose observables compute defect one-point functions $a_\mathcal{O}$ of BPS bulk primaries?
\item Which defect anomaly coefficients (such as the $b$-anomaly of $2d$ defects in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories, or the $4d$ defect anomalies in $6d$ $(2,0)$ theories) can be extracted from the localized partition function or its derivatives, and through which precise formulas?
\item Can the defect free energy (or $g$-function) and the corresponding monotonicity ($b$-theorem, defect $a$-theorem) be proven non-perturbatively for supersymmetric defects via localization?
\item Can localization, possibly combined with integrability or the conformal bootstrap, determine non-protected defect CFT data such as anomalous dimensions of non-BPS defect primaries and bulk-to-defect OPE coefficients at finite coupling?
\end{enumerate}
artifact.category_tag: Boundary and defect conformal field theory
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: supersymmetric localization yields exact matrix-model expressions for one-point functions of BPS operators in the presence of D5-type interfaces in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, exact bulk-defect OPE data for the 1/2-BPS Wilson line (in combination with the Quantum Spectral Curve), and exact results for protected correlators in 3d $\mathcal{N}\ge 4$ defect setups. Defect $b$- and $a$-anomalies have been computed via localization in several supersymmetric examples, and a general defect $a$-theorem framework using $a$-maximization has been developed. However, a complete non-perturbative determination of all defect CFT data (including non-BPS spectra and general anomaly monotonicity theorems) via localization remains open; the broad question is therefore only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Non-perturbative defect one-point functions in planar N=4 SYM
status_evidence.snippet: An effective 2d defect-Yang-Mills theory derived from supersymmetric localization gives a matrix model for defect one-point functions, with exact results in the 't Hooft coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Localization yields non-perturbative defect one-point functions for D5-type interfaces in planar N=4 SYM.

status_evidence.title: More Exact Results in the Wilson Loop Defect CFT: Bulk-Defect OPE
status_evidence.snippet: Bulk-defect structure constants at finite 't Hooft coupling for the 1/2-BPS Wilson line, expressed via Q-functions of the Quantum Spectral Curve.
status_evidence.claim: Exact bulk-defect OPE coefficients are obtained for the 1/2-BPS Wilson line defect CFT.

status_evidence.title: On protected defect correlators in 3d N>=4 theories
status_evidence.snippet: Localization computes protected defect correlators in 3d theories with eight or more supercharges.
status_evidence.claim: Localization gives exact protected defect correlators in 3d N>=4 theories.

status_evidence.title: Defect a-theorem and a-maximization
status_evidence.snippet: A defect a-theorem framework using a-maximization for supersymmetric defects.
status_evidence.claim: Supersymmetric methods provide non-perturbative control over defect anomalies and RG monotonicity.

status_evidence.title: Boundary and defect CFT: open problems and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open questions on what supersymmetric localization can teach us about bCFTs and dCFTs.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of what additional non-perturbative information SUSY/localization can give about bCFTs/dCFTs is posed as open.
